accepted.reason: Reviewed as genuine domain-specific meanings: HTML defines document markup units, Arrays defines a value at an indexed position, and DOM defines a node representing an HTML element. They do not contradict.
Compatible depth difference: How Websites Work defines the general server message, while Fetch API Basics defines JavaScript's Response object that represents such an HTTP response.
Genuine homonym: HTML Document Structure defines the document metadata element, while Git defines the current branch or directly referenced commit.
Genuine homonym: Forms uses label for control-identifying text and markup; Domains uses label for a dot-separated segment of a domain name.
Reviewed as compatible context-specific meanings: form-control data, a CSS declaration setting, JavaScript data, and data associated with an object property are all correct in their owning lessons.
Genuine homonym: CSS declares a presentation property and its value, while JavaScript Variables declares a binding name.
Genuine homonym: CSS uses property for a named presentation feature; JavaScript Objects uses property for a key-value association.
Genuine domain-specific meanings: Cascade uses origin for a stylesheet source category; Cookies and Storage uses origin for a scheme-host-port browser security boundary.
Compatible specialization: Arrays teaches bracket notation for indexed elements, while Objects teaches the same square-bracket form for property access using an expression.
Genuine homonym: Accessibility uses role for an interface object's semantics; GitHub uses role for a collection of repository permissions.
